title: IMDb Preprocessing Study
subtitle: Text Preprocessing in Neural Text Classifiers
description: An unofficial, reproducible re-run of a BlackboxNLP 2018 paper's IMDb experiments: four ways to preprocess the text, two neural models, every run traceable. It started as research for my master's thesis in 2019. That version had three bugs; this one fixes them and says where they were.
longDescription: Does it matter whether you lowercase, lemmatize or group multiword expressions before training a neural text classifier? Camacho-Collados and Pilehvar measured it in On the Role of Text Preprocessing in Neural Network Architectures (BlackboxNLP 2018). This repository re-implements the IMDb part of that study: pick one of four preprocessing variants (vanilla, lowercased, lemmatized, multiword) and one of two models (CNN or CNN+LSTM), and preproc-imdb trains on the 25,000 training reviews and reports the accuracy on the 25,000 test reviews. Every run leaves a folder with its settings, library versions, training history and every prediction. It started in 2019 as a Python 3 port of the authors' sensecnn code for my master's research, and was rewritten in 2026 on Keras 3.15 and TensorFlow 2.21, fixing three bugs in the 2019 port.
imageCaptions: Two models, one trunk: embedding and Conv1D, then global max pool, or pool plus BiLSTM
features: Four preprocessing variants: vanilla, lowercased, lemmatized and multiword
The paper's two models: CNN and CNN+LSTM
Trains on the 25,000 IMDb training reviews and tests on the other 25,000
Every run saves its settings, library versions, training history and predictions
Fixed seeds, so the same setup gives the same accuracy again
Pinned Keras and TensorFlow versions, with a Docker option
challenges: The 2019 port had three bugs that quietly changed the numbers
Every number in the results table had to be traceable to a run
solutions: Rebuilt word ids, embedding rows and early stopping, and documented each 2019 bug next to its fix
Each run writes a folder with its settings, versions, history and every prediction
results: A results table that puts this repository's accuracy next to the paper's for every variant and model
Close to the paper on CNN+LSTM, for example 88.6 against 88.9 on the vanilla text
why: My master's research needed to know whether lowercasing, lemmatizing or joining multiword phrases changes what a neural sentiment model learns, so I re-ran a paper's IMDb experiments. In the rerun, changing the random seed moved accuracy more than changing the preprocessing did.
gains: For anyone wondering whether lowercasing or lemmatizing is worth it: pick a variant and a model, get an accuracy traceable to a folder, and compare it with the paper. Your own preprocessing needs four text files, one command and patience: a CNN+LSTM run takes 13 to 19 minutes on CPU.
lessons: The 2019 port numbered words 'count + 2', so words with the same count shared an id and the most frequent words became unknown.
The 2019 port also stopped early on the test set; the rewrite trains 3 epochs by default, like the authors' code.
Fine-tuning hides missing vectors: on vanilla text the lowercased embeddings covered 13,265 of 19,998 words, yet accuracy barely moved.
